title: Why She Paid $500 for the Rock That Hit Her
sources: Encyclopedia of Alabama, 'Hodges Meteorite Strike (Sylacauga Aerolite)': on November 30, 1954, a meteorite crashed through the roof of Ann Hodges' rented house in Oak Grove near Sylacauga, Alabama, bounced off a console radio and struck her as she napped on the couch, leaving a large bruise; landlady Birdie (Bertie) Guy claimed the rock; the Hodgeses settled by paying her $500; the fragment was later donated to the Alabama Museum of Natural History
Wikipedia, 'Ann Elizabeth Fowler Hodges' (Hodges fragment 3.86 kg / 8.5 lb; struck her upper thigh/hip and hand; first documented case of a person injured by a meteorite)
Astronomy.com, 'Nov. 30, 1954: The first known human injury via a meteorite'
National Geographic (2013), Ann Hodges meteorite strike
